title: What one Carolina Reaper did to a man's brain 🌶️
subject: pepper
description:
Would you take one bite? 👇

Why does a Carolina Reaper feel like fire, and what happened to the 34-year-old who ate one at a pepper contest in New York? The first reported case of reversible cerebral vasoconstriction syndrome linked to the pepper. Not medical advice.

Sources: Boddhula et al., BMJ Case Reports, April 2018 (doi 10.1136/bcr-2017-224085), via Medscape and Sci.News; Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine 2021 press release (David Julius); Scientific American
tags: what happens if you eat a carolina reaper

scenes.text: Eat a Carolina Reaper, and your nerves report a fire.
Its capsaicin trips your real heat sensor, a discovery that won David Julius the 2021 Nobel Prize.
Nothing is burning, yet you sweat and your nose runs.
In 2018, a 34-year-old ate one at a New York contest. Dry heaves came first, then neck pain.
Then thunderclap headaches. Scans showed arteries in his brain had narrowed.
His was the first case tied to the pepper. 5 weeks later, his arteries were normal again.
